label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Hi Mikaela, no worries at all, happy to give you the real version. Grant you might as well read this too.

We've got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds, and we started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept once mating had kicked off. We skip the Tues, Thurs, Sat and Sun arvo milkings, so 4 once-a-days a week. Mornings are 5.15 every day no matter what.

**Production:** going off the Fonterra app we're down about 6% on the same weeks last year. Our rep told us to expect 8-10% so it's come in better than he said. Still a hit though, and you need to be able to wear it.

**Cells:** they didn't go mental but they did jump. We were sitting at 110k and it went up to about 180k for the first 3 weeks. It's come back to around 135k now, so it's settling but not back to where it was. That's the thing I'd most want you to know. On the skip days you have to be right on top of teat spraying and actually walk through the cows and look at them. If you get slack, it bites you.

It bit us once. We had a heifer whose mastitis went bad on a skipped arvo and we didn't pick it up till the next morning. She lost a quarter. That was on us, but it shows how quickly things can get away on you when there's a big gap between milkings. We're a lot more careful now.

**The good stuff:** lame cows are way down. We've got 4 on the lame list now and this time last year we had 11. Our back paddocks are a 1.8km walk, so cutting out that trip 4 times a week makes a real difference to their feet.

The cows adjusted quicker than I expected. They bellowed at the gate for about 4 days, then they were fine and haven't bothered since.

For us the biggest change has been the people side. On the first skipped Sunday arvo Dave and I drove to Hamilton to see the grandkids. That was the first Sunday off in spring we've had in 20-odd years and I'm not ashamed to say I got a bit teary. Kieran our 2IC told me the other day it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. With your young fella already talking about leaving over the hours, I'd give that a lot of weight. And if Tom's knees are as bad as you say, having those arvos off will probably help him more than anything else you could change.

Honestly I wouldn't go back. For us the hours alone are worth the 6%. But I'd be lying if I said there's no downside. You lose some milk, the cells go up at the start, and you can't relax on the skip days. If you go in knowing all that I reckon you'll be fine. I just don't want you thinking it's all roses and then cursing me come March.

Come and have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th. I'll bring them along and you can pull them apart. Or just give me a ring whenever, it's much easier than typing all this out on my phone 😂

Bev
